title: Canonical abutment maps and graded isomorphisms for a truncation couple
statement: theorem truncation_canonical_abutment {A : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} A] [Abelian A] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v₁} A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w₁} A] {B : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} B] [Abelian B] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v₂} B] [HasDerivedCategory.{w₂} B] (F : A ⥤ B) [F.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits F] (K : CochainComplex.Plus A) (a : ℤ) (ha : ∀ q : ℤ, q < a → IsZero (K.obj.homology q)) (X : BigradedExactCouple B 0) (hD : X.D = TruncationCouple.D F K) (hE : X.E = TruncationCouple.E F K) (halpha : (∀ p q : ℤ, X.alpha p q = eqToHom (by rw [hD]) ≫ TruncationCouple.alpha F K p q ≫ eqToHom (by rw [hD]))) (hf : (∀ p q : ℤ, X.f p q = eqToHom (by rw [hE]) ≫ TruncationCouple.f F K p q ≫ eqToHom (by rw [hD]))) (hg : (∀ p q : ℤ, X.initialG p q = eqToHom (by rw [hD]) ≫ TruncationCouple.g F K p q ≫ eqToHom (by rw [hE]))) (hDzero : ∀ p q : ℤ, q < a → IsZero (X.D p q)) (hEzero : ∀ p q : ℤ, (p < 0 ∨ q < a) → IsZero (X.E p q)) : ∃ (inc : ∀ (r : ℕ) (p q : ℤ), (X.pageCouple r).D p q ⟶ X.D p q) (L : X.LimitSubobjects) (H : ℤ → B) (hH : H = fun n : ℤ ↦ (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B n).obj (F.rightDerivedFunctor.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K.obj))) (j : ∀ n q : ℤ, X.D (n - q) q ⟶ H n) (c : ∀ n : ℤ, X.D 0 n ⟶ H n) (FA : ∀ n : ℤ, DecreasingFiltration (X.D 0 n)) (FH : ∀ n : ℤ, DecreasingFiltration (H n)), (∀ p q : ℤ, inc 0 p q = 𝟙 _) ∧ (∀ (r : ℕ) (p q : ℤ), inc (r + 1) p q = (X.pageCouple r).derivedDInclusion p q ≫ inc r p q) ∧ (∀ p q : ℤ, L.Z p q = X.cycleBoundaryTower.Z ((max 2 (max (q - a + 2) (p + 1))).toNat - 2) p q ∧ L.B p q = X.cycleBoundaryTower.B ((max 2 (max (q - a + 2) (p + 1))).toNat - 2) p q ∧ Nonempty (X.pageInfinity L p q ≅ X.page (max 2 (max (q - a + 2) (p + 1))).toNat p q)) ∧ (∀ n q : ℤ, j n q = eqToHom (by rw [hD]; unfold TruncationCouple.D; congr 1; omega) ≫ (TruncationCouple.bridgeIso F (TruncationCouple.truncation K q) n).inv ≫ (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B n).map (F.rightDerivedFunctor.map (DerivedCategory.Q.map (K.obj.ιTruncLE q))) ≫ eqToHom (by rw [hH])) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, c n = eqToHom (by congr 1; omega) ≫ j n n) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, IsIso (c n)) ∧ (∀ n p : ℤ, 0 ≤ p → (FA n).step p = imageSubobject (X.incomingAlphaIter p.toNat 0 n)) ∧ (∀ n p : ℤ, p ≤ 0 → (FA n).step p = ⊤) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, FH n = (FA n).image (c n)) ∧ (∀ n p : ℤ, (FH n).step p = imageSubobject (j n (n - p))) ∧ (∀ n p : ℤ, p ≤ 0 → (FH n).step p = ⊤) ∧ (∀ n p : ℤ, n - a + 1 ≤ p → (FH n).step p = ⊥) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, (FH n).IsFinite ∧ (FH n).IsExhaustive ∧ (FH n).IsSeparated ∧ BigradedExactCouple.IsInverseLimit (FH n)) ∧ (∀ p q : ℤ, p < 0 → IsZero ((FH (p + q)).gradedPiece p) ∧ IsZero (X.pageInfinity L p q)) ∧ (∀ (p q : ℤ) (hp : 0 ≤ p), ∃ (lambda : X.D 0 (p + q) ⟶ X.D (p - max (p + 3) (q - a + 2) + 2) (q + max (p + 3) (q - a + 2) - 2)) (lift : ((FA (p + q)).step p : B) ⟶ (X.pageCouple ((max (p + 3) (q - a + 2)).toNat - 2)).D (p - max (p + 3) (q - a + 2) + 2) (q + max (p + 3) (q - a + 2) - 2)) (psi : (FA (p + q)).gradedPiece p ≅ X.page (max (p + 3) (q - a + 2)).toNat p q) (grc : (FA (p + q)).gradedPiece p ≅ (FH (p + q)).gradedPiece p) (stable : X.page (max (p + 3) (q - a + 2)).toNat p q ≅ X.pageInfinity L p q) (Theta : (FH (p + q)).gradedPiece p ≅ X.pageInfinity L p q) (cStep : ((FA (p + q)).step p : B) ⟶ ((FH (p + q)).step p : B)) (hZ : X.cycleBoundaryTower.Z ((max (p + 3) (q - a + 2)).toNat - 2) p q = L.Z p q), IsIso lambda ∧ lambda = X.alphaIter (-(p - max (p + 3) (q - a + 2) + 2)).toNat 0 (p + q) ≫ eqToHom (by congr 1 <;> omega) ∧ IsIso lift ∧ lift ≫ inc ((max (p + 3) (q - a + 2)).toNat - 2) (p - max (p + 3) (q - a + 2) + 2) (q + max (p + 3) (q - a + 2) - 2) = ((FA (p + q)).step p).arrow ≫ lambda ∧ cStep ≫ ((FH (p + q)).step p).arrow = ((FA (p + q)).step p).arrow ≫ c (p + q) ∧ cStep ≫ cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE ((FH (p + q)).step (p + 1)) ((FH (p + q)).step p) ((FH (p + q)).antitone_step (by omega))) = cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE ((FA (p + q)).step (p + 1)) ((FA (p + q)).step p) ((FA (p + q)).antitone_step (by omega))) ≫ grc.hom ∧ X.cycleBoundaryTower.projection ((max (p + 3) (q - a + 2)).toNat - 2) p q ≫ stable.hom = eqToHom (congrArg (fun S : Subobject (X.E p q) ↦ (S : B)) hZ) ≫ cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE (L.B p q) (L.Z p q) (X.limitBoundary_le_cycle L p q)) ∧ cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE ((FA (p + q)).step (p + 1)) ((FA (p + q)).step p) ((FA (p + q)).antitone_step (by omega))) ≫ psi.hom = lift ≫ (X.pageCouple ((max (p + 3) (q - a + 2)).toNat - 2)).g (p - max (p + 3) (q - a + 2) + 2) (q + max (p + 3) (q - a + 2) - 2) ≫ eqToHom (by unfold BigradedExactCouple.page; congr 1 <;> omega) ∧ Theta = grc.symm ≪≫ psi ≪≫ stable) ∧ ∃ (AH : ∀ n : ℤ, X.AlphaColimit n) (hAH : ∀ n : ℤ, (AH n).obj = H n), (∀ n p : ℤ, (AH n).ι p ≫ eqToHom (hAH n) = eqToHom (by congr 1; omega) ≫ j n (n - p)) ∧ X.ConvergesTo L AH

proof.text: Construct the iterated D inclusions recursively from the derived-D inclusions. Obtain limiting subobjects from halfPlaneConvergence. Sharp stabilization and monotonicity show, by the greatest-lower-bound and least-upper-bound properties, that these limit subobjects equal the sharp stationary cycles and boundaries. The cycle-tower projection is epic with kernel the boundary inclusion, so its cokernel is the finite page; transport the quotient along these subobject equalities to identify the infinite and sharp finite pages.

source.place: proof, steps 5--7; Lean refinement with the same objects and canonical maps

proof.text: Apply truncation_abutment_cocone to obtain the explicitly prescribed H,j,c, the invertibility of c, and its diagonal cocone and positive incoming-alpha normalization equations. Apply the proved abstract abutment_image_filtration to this cocone and the chosen L. It constructs FA,FH, all image and support equations, the finite inverse-limit filtration, the negative graded/infinite-page vanishing, and the prescribed diagonal colimit with convergence.

proof.text: Apply abutment_finite_page_comparison to the recursive inclusions, sharp limit-subobject equalities and the incoming-alpha/image filtrations. This supplies the positive-bidegree lambda,lift,psi,grc,stable,Theta,cStep,hZ and their equations. Assemble these witnesses with the previously proved normalization, stabilization, filtration and colimit clauses, preserving the original statement exactly.
